source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 9: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer:
For this scenario, do not choose tensor or pipeline parallelism from a generic rule. First state the latency SLA (including p99), throughput and concurrency target, model checkpoint and sequence-length distribution, GPU count/type, memory budget, interconnect topology, software/driver/runtime versions, availability objective, and whether reconfiguration is allowed. Treat the following as assumptions to verify rather than facts: model, tokenizer, request trace, decoding, placement, power limits, scheduler, batching policy, and load generator are fixed; only the parallelism strategy and preregistered partition/microbatch settings vary.

Define a numerical, falsifiable hypothesis for scenario variant 9: at the declared offered load, one strategy will have lower p99 end-to-end latency (and state the margin) while meeting quality, error-rate, memory, and availability gates. Use a randomized interleaved controlled experiment with identical requests, equal warm-up/compilation, fixed sample size, exclusion and stopping rules, and disjoint tuning and held-out workloads. Compare feasible layer partitions and pipeline microbatch counts, and record per-GPU memory/utilization, communication bytes and time, synchronization waits, pipeline bubbles, queueing, TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency, requests/s and tokens/s, energy/cost, errors, timeouts, OOMs, stragglers, failed-rank recovery, and reconfiguration time, all with units and raw per-request data. Stratify by sequence length, batch/concurrency, topology, and controlled failure injection; report confidence intervals and identify thermal drift, placement, load-shape, cache, compiler, and straggler confounders.

Select the measured winner only if all preregistered gates and uncertainty bounds pass; otherwise retain the baseline or report no decision. Canary any change with authorization, isolation, rate limits, redaction, and monitoring. Roll back to the versioned known-good configuration on SLA/quality/safety regression, instability, failed-rank recovery, unauthorized data exposure, or resource leakage. Evidence required: signed configurations and authorization, topology and partition manifests, disjoint workload manifests, raw synchronized traces, failure/recovery logs, confidence intervals, and a tested rollback record; do not claim platform-specific support without measurement.
risks: tensor communication and pipeline bubbles can trade off differently across topology and microbatch settings
queueing, cache state, thermal drift, compiler effects, and stragglers can confound latency comparisons
failure injection and recovery measurements may not represent all production fault modes

disjoint tuning and held-out workload manifests with randomized paired raw metrics and units
per-rank communication, synchronization, queueing, latency, resource, and failure/recovery traces
